selection: Soot-derived I/O and coverage; no manually declared fault site
qualification: A fault-induced exact throw counts even if DFSClient later clears its key and retries successfully. It must still be distinguishable from the original JUnit's deliberate stale-client-key rejection, by an additional throw or independent causal path evidence. A JUnit assertion failure alone does not qualify.
excluded_reason: The original JUnit obtains and retains a client encryption key, clears server keys, waits until every DataNode lacks that key ID, then starts pipeline recovery. Thus its first client handshake is expected to throw the exact missing-key exception without injected faults. The audited RPC-fault trials show one client-initiated handshake throw after this wait, followed by key refresh. Successful retry is not the exclusion criterion; the deliberate preexisting stale key is. No second or independently attributable exact throw was observed.

rpc_fault_target_cooccurrences_not_detec.faults: Two java.io.IOException injections at data7 sendHeartBeat replies; the first reply carried KeyUpdateCommand.
rpc_fault_target_cooccurrences_not_detec.why_not_attributed: The target was on a different DataNode, after the JUnit verified its original cached client key was absent on all DataNodes.

rpc_fault_target_cooccurrences_not_detec.faults: Four consecutive java.io.IOException injections at data1 sendHeartBeat replies, three carrying KeyUpdateCommand.
rpc_fault_target_cooccurrences_not_detec.why_not_attributed: Despite matching the faulted node, this was the first client DataStreamer SASL handshake after the JUnit waited for all DataNodes to lose its deliberately stale cached key; only one exact throw occurred.

raw_attempt_log_audit.audit_rule: For every exact allKeys missing-key message in an archived attempt log, the same key ID appears later in DataStreamer.continueRetryingOrThrow, which states that the client will fetch a new encryption key and retry.

excluded_first_target_timing.timing_limit: The trace records event order but no per-event wall timestamp; the DataXceiver error log is a close proxy for the exact throw.
